entry.title: Weeknote #2027
entry.content:
Random googling's this week:

  • is that kirsten dunst singing in spider man 3 (it is!)
  • circle pokemon
  • king charles podcast tweet

I was on the fence about GTA Vi. It's been years since the last one, do I still care about such games? Turns out I watched one review, immediately preordered the game, and also bought a new monitor. It has allowed me to live out my fantasy of completing all the maintenance jobs on my home. The rest of the game is good too. I think it might be the first time a child has been shown in a GTA game which is notable.

A McNugget number is a number "that can be obtained by adding together orders of McDonald's Chicken McNuggets" (6, 9, and 20 boxes). There are only 22 non-McNugget numbers with 43 being the largest. (via Sara)

I also learned about Malaphors, or at least, learned that a word exists for such things. A malaphor is the mixing of two common sayings like "We'll burn that bridge when we come to it" or "Burning the midnight oil at both ends".

Stephen Hackett has an app out for making adding reminders to Apple Reminders better. Apple set the bar pretty low but he's done a great job with this.

Adam has finally got NeatStats, his take on analytics, out the door and ready for sign ups. It has widgets, a nice dashboard, decent privacy, excellent pricing. I plan to move the sites I track over to it soon.

This video was really helpful so I could fix a loose cap on a LAMY Safari that I had. Kind of odd to have diagrams in a video when a web page would be so much better but I am an old so whatever. 67 frfr.

Maybe it's nothing, maybe it's something, but SocialSpec at looks promising.

Folksy is a UK alternative to Etsy. Neat, especially as Etsy is forcing AI training on it's sellers with no opt-out.

Another SVG logo repository has appeared, called Logos. Added to my toolkit. Speaking of which, I added Myinstants which is a soundboard site that has a lot of stuff I always seem to need and they're easily downloadable.

Linnet is a little menu bar music player for Apple Music. Cute.

Allo is a new variable font thats variable in every dimension you can imagine and it's free. The work thats gone into this is wild.

Search Browser is a minimal browser for MacOS focused on speed.

Finally I've found myself reading How I use Obsidian by Steph Ango again because my vault is becoming unwieldy and I think it would work better for me with a bit more structure.

entry.title: Finger Lickin' Doom
entry.content:
For the latest episode of Ruminate I tried the Doom burger at KFC. We spoke at length about the greenness of it all on the episode, which I think it's worth your time, especially if you're new to the show. When I was prepping for the show I had an idea to mashup the Avengers theme song with the Beastie Boys track, Finger Lickin' Good.

I've never done a mashup before but I was able to change the tempo of the Avengers theme to match closer to the Beastie Boys track, as well as extracted the vocals using lalal.ai and make something I quite like. I even did a cover for it because why not — finding a photo of the Colonel with two other friends was harder than expected. The font I used is Fresh Marker which is pretty close to the original.

Download MP3

entry.title: Knowember
entry.content:
Knowember is an idea by Robert Birming; “one page to let others know a bit more about yourself - the same set of questions for everyone.”. Here we go.

A photo

I love this photo I took in Edinburgh in 2022 for reason I can't quite explain.

Name or nickname

I had some questionable nicknames in my teenage years, none of which I'm willing to post here. However Robb, with two Bs, is my actual legal[1] name because I changed it. Why two Bs? That is a good story.

Where in the world I blog from

Since having kids, I mostly write from my phone in Obsidian, although I still keep posting proper blog posts as a big computer activity with my custom CMS that is basically a front-end for editing files on Forgejo.

Since writing this paragraph, I realise this was about location so: Portsmouth mostly.

What my blog is mostly about

There is no mostly anything. It started with lots of reviews of apps I wrote at AppAdvice, then lots of grumpy links about tech, then around 2012 I started doing what I should have always done and just posted whatever I felt like. It goes in phases, like my interests — my site is never going to be "about" a thing because I'm a full human being with many interests and I'm fickle[2]. At the moment? Retro Cameras and Analogue tools.

  1. England has no concept of legal names — if you knew me as crapbag and I went by that name, then that is a perfectly valid name. "Legal" in most senses means "What's on your passport". ⤾

  2. And tired. Always tired. ⤾

entry.title: Jaffa Cake Jaffa Cam Review
entry.content:
As a novelty camera enjoyer, I had to get my hands on a Jaffa Cake Jaffa cam. Just look at it.

For a penny short of seven english pounds you get the camera, the keyring, a USB A to C cable (A, really?), and a pack of Jaffa Cakes. You do have to provide your own micro SD card.

On turning it on you get a little jingle and a Jaffa Cake splash screen. Cute. I stuck in a 1GB one I had lying around and it said I could fit around 7500 images on it which gives you some idea of how low quality these photos are going to be — or maybe McVities have cracked a new compression algorithm that will change the world? Sadly, it's the former. The photos are 1920×1440.

Each of these photos, along with the other ones I took, I was as steady as I could be and the light was decent. I'm starting to think these types of cameras exist purely to disprove "the best camera is the one you have with you". I reckon I could draw better representations of these moments.

The camera also has filters, which I didn't use for any photos worth sharing, including a santa one and a beach scene but no jaffa cake one. What are they even doing here? Useless.

Interestingly the B&M camera that Ben has appears to be more or less the exact same camera based on the UI and version number formatting. You shouldn't buy that one either.

The only conclusion to be drawn is that £7 isn't enough to get a good camera. The Jaffa Cakes were good though.
entry.summary: Jaffa Cake made a camera for some reasons so I bought it

entry.title: Fixing Illustrations on a Dark Background with CSS
entry.content:
If you've visited my site recently you might have noticed some illustrations I've done appear on some pages, notably the home page and my 404 page. I wanted to use this brick drawing I did for Inktober but on the dark mode background is doesn't look good:

My first thought was to just get rid of dark mode completely and just have light mode. I spoke to a handful of people about it and came to the conclusion that this was an extreme solution. Also, I like dark mode in general so it seems stupid to nuke it just for this.

I tried a handful of different things like changing the line colour to white and just loading the correct version depending on the theme. This worked, but still looked shit on dark mode. I tried some other things like adding an outline or even a thicker line like a sticker might have but all of them had the same problem — I would need to make two versions of every drawing which I really didn't want to do.

I had a vague recollection of being able to do a drop shadow on transparent PNGs and after some digging I found it can be done with filter and drop-shadow. Stacking two drop shadows give the best outline for what I wanted.

filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1px #ececec) drop-shadow(0 0 1px #ececec);

It's not perfect but it does the job, especially on drawings that have a more defined outline like the hats.

Now I can start adding some more illustrations I've got lined up for the site.
entry.summary: A solution to dark-outlined drawings on dark mode on my website

entry.title: Remove Valance Endcaps from Primrose Awning
entry.content:
Warning: boring homeowner awning post.

The valance on my awning had come off the runner and was hanging out the end of the awning casing so I need to get the endcaps off. The instructions that came with it don’t mention the valance or end caps at all, and everything I saw online suggested there should be screws holding them in but there wasn’t.

I extended the awning slightly and shoved my phone camera in there to see what was going on and it turns out on full cassette awnings, the endcaps are held on with a 10mm bolt from the inside. Once I loosened the bolt, I was able to get the end cap off and rethread the valance.
entry.summary: This wasn’t obvious to me and I’ll definitely forget in the future

entry.title: Fix Kindle Stuck in Sign In Loop
entry.content:
I recently bought my wife a new Kindle so I grabbed her old one to sign into my account. I put my username and password in, then it would ask for my 2FA code which I would enter and it would always go back to the sign in screen again. I did this thrice before moving onto other fixes.

I tried all the usual troubleshooting like updating it, checking the time and date was correct, and nothing worked. Then I recalled my old Xbox not being able to sign in if 2FA was on I turned it off and it worked. Why it's prompting for a 2FA code if it doesn't support it I'll never know.

Anyway, back to never finding time to read and yes, I turned 2FA back on.
entry.summary: A stupid fix to something I wasted an hour on

entry.content:
Doing...

I hand-delivered the final drawing for St Jude this morning and we're almost halfway through Inktober — I am furious to confirm that practicing actually works and does indeed improve your skills. Some of the art I've done in the past month I'm properly proud of. Jim loved his so much, he framed it.

The Knightlings have been ill on and off for the past month while the weather can't make it's mind up. We've had a couple of hospital visits as well — one for scary breathing-related things and one because Baby Knight the first is clumsy af and had to have her head glued back together.

A few weeks later, the same nurse who did the aforementioned gluing also fixed my finger when I sliced it open sideways with a Stanley knife[1]. Can't imagine why my children are so clumsy, could come from anywhere.

Eagle-eyed people might have noticed I added a single illustration to the home page of some hats. I have some more I'm going to add in the next few weeks.

I've not made much progress with the self-hosted version of EchoFeed but I do have a solid plan so that should be happening soon. I want to make it as easy as possible to self-host it.

I've made a minimal (~10 lines of CSS, !10 lines of JS) image gallery using the dialog element to showcase the St Jude drawings once they arrive with everyone who donated.

Listening...

  • Still going through Connor Price's back catalog including the tracks he's done with Nic D
  • Czarface Meets Frankie Pulitzer. Frankie Pulitzer is Tom Hardy, which was news to me and he goes hard.
  • Unshatter by Linkin Park. Emily Armstrong was such a great choice.
  • Ekoh, Lø Spirit & Ninth Key are dropping banger after banger in their 2000s-era Linkin Park style. I love it.

Watching...

We've been rewatching My Name is Earl and it's so wholesome. I wasn't sure if it would hold up given when it was made but it really does. It's a damn shame it never got it's final season to wrap everything up.

I'm two episodes into the new Reacher and I'm into it.

entry.title: St Jude 2026 Recap
entry.content:
Here we are, a week into extended September and Relay's annual fundraiser has come to a close with over $750k raised — and nearly $9k of that came from mine and Adam's campaign.

This is short of our goal of $15k that I set without really thinking much about it and it is lower than previous years. A couple of people reached out privately to apologise that they couldn't donate this year — it's rough out there. I haven't donated as much as previous years either for various reasons but to raise nearly $9k is nothing short of amazing. Everyone who shared the campaign or donated, even a small amount, thank you.

We did our usual offering of stickers this year, which expanded from a two pack into a four pack, then we added Jimothy. I offered my drawings again and once I have them all complete I will have done 32 of them, five more than last year. I'll put up a post once they've all arrived because I remembered to scan them all this year. Finally Adam decided to make his life difficult and offer friendship bracelets — he has 20 or so of these to make. Good luck.

I've started my note of ideas for next year — it's basically September already.

entry.title: My Inktober Setup
entry.content:
It's Inktober again which means I'm drawing one thing a day, in ink, from the official[1] prompt list. I'm tagging my posts with #Inktober and #Inktober2026 — these tag pages are flagged to render the images in a gallery instead of the usual notes pages. My first drawing is up as of this morning.

As much as I love Jeff the dinosaur from last year[2] it's too easy to fall back on "Jeff does/interacts with whatever the prompt is" so this year will be mostly Jeff-free. Last year my drawings were all over the place in terms of size so this year I bought a 12x12 Sakura sketchbook — I'll be using this exclusively for Inktober for the next few years. Unlike last year when I used Uni Pins, I'm a big Sakura Micron boy now. I talk more about this on this week's episode of The Pen Addict which will be out in a few hours.

One of the things with projects like this is I want to be consistent with how I'm posting stuff. Last year I would have to go back to the previous days post to see if I did a full stop or colon after the day number, did I put the prompt in quotes, what about the filename? So I set up two Alfred snippets — one for the filename and one for the post itself. Snippets is a feature I use a lot for other things.

# INKtober Filename
;inkf
# raw
inktober-2026-{date:dd}-
# becomes
inktober-2026-01-

# INKtober Post
;inkp
# raw
Day {date:dd} - {cursor}

![](https://cdn.rknight.me/site/2026/inktober-2026-{date:dd}-.jpg)
#becomes
Day 01 - 

![](https://cdn.rknight.me/site/2026/inktober-2026-01-.jpg)

  1. I've heard some not great things about the official folks and "licensing" the name but nothing substantial so I'm sticking with it ⤾

  2. And let's not even talk about Knobgate ⤾
entry.summary: My setup for Inktober this year
